messages.content: I’ll inspect the staged directory first, then sample the files enough to infer the schema and produce one timestamped Polars frame.

The upload is a mix of health exports, notes/messages, calendar, transactions, pharmacy fills, and genotype snippets. I’m sampling each format now so the parser can preserve timestamps and keep the final table coherent.

The final shape should be an event stream rather than a forced daily join: each Apple/Oura/message/journal/visit/fill/transaction/calendar/genotype observation gets its own `timestamp`, with source-specific columns populated. That keeps precision without inventing false joins across unrelated records.

function.arguments:
{"code": "from pathlib import Path
import json, re, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import polars as pl
root=Path(DATA_DIR)
rows=[]
for p in sorted(root.iterdir()):
    text = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    rows.append({'file': p.name, 'size_bytes': p.stat().st_size, 'lines': text.count('\n')+1, 'first_chars': text[:120].replace('\n','\\n')})
# apple tag/type counts
apple = root/'apple_health_export.xml'
record_types={}
tag_counts={}
for event, elem in ET.iterparse(apple, events=('end',)):
    tag_counts[elem.tag]=tag_counts.get(elem.tag,0)+1
    if elem.tag=='Record':
        t=elem.attrib.get('type','')
        record_types[t]=record_types.get(t,0)+1
    elem.clear()
for k,v in tag_counts.items():
    rows.append({'file':'apple_health_export.xml', 'size_bytes':None, 'lines':None, 'first_chars':f'tag_count {k}: {v}'})
for k,v in sorted(record_types.items()):
    rows.append({'file':'apple_health_export.xml', 'size_bytes':None, 'lines':None, 'first_chars':f'record_type {k}: {v}'})
# json top counts
oura=json.loads((root/'oura_sleep_raw.json').read_text())
rows.append({'file':'oura_sleep_raw.json','size_bytes':None,'lines':None,'first_chars':f"sleep records: {len(oura.get('sleep',{}).get('data',[]))}"})
first=oura.get('sleep',{}).get('data',[{}])[0]
rows.append({'file':'oura_sleep_raw.json','size_bytes':None,'lines':None,'first_chars':'first sleep keys: '+', '.join(first.keys())})
rows.append({'file':'oura_sleep_raw.json','size_bytes':None,'lines':None,'first_chars':f"first HR items: {len(first.get('heart_rate',{}).get('items',[]))}, movement items: {len(first.get('movement_30_sec',{}).get('items',[])) if isinstance(first.get('movement_30_sec'),dict) else 'n/a'}"})
plaid=json.loads((root/'plaid_transactions.json').read_text())
rows.append({'file':'plaid_transactions.json','size_bytes':None,'lines':None,'first_chars':f"accounts: {len(plaid.get('accounts',[]))}, transactions: {len(plaid.get('transactions',[]))}"})
result_df=pl.DataFrame(rows)"}

messages.content: I found the large files are structured enough to parse directly: Apple Health is XML with Record/Workout/ActivitySummary/StateOfMind elements, Oura is nested JSON with nightly summaries and time-series heart-rate samples, and the rest are compact text/CSV/JSON exports. Next I’m checking counts and edge cases before writing the full parser.

import json, re, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import polars as pl
root=Path(DATA_DIR)
print('FILES')
for p in sorted(root.iterdir()):
    print(p.name, p.stat().st_size, 'bytes')
print('\nAPPLE TAGS / RECORD TYPES')
tag_counts={}; record_types={}; workout_types={}; som_kinds={}
for event, elem in ET.iterparse(root/'apple_health_export.xml', events=('end',)):
    tag_counts[elem.tag]=tag_counts.get(elem.tag,0)+1
    if elem.tag=='Record': record_types[elem.attrib.get('type','')]=record_types.get(elem.attrib.get('type',''),0)+1
    if elem.tag=='Workout': workout_types[elem.attrib.get('workoutActivityType','')]=workout_types.get(elem.attrib.get('workoutActivityType',''),0)+1
    if elem.tag=='StateOfMind': som_kinds[elem.attrib.get('kind','')]=som_kinds.get(elem.attrib.get('kind',''),0)+1
    elem.clear()
print('tag_counts', tag_counts)
print('record_types')
for k,v in sorted(record_types.items()): print(k, v)
print('workout_types', workout_types)
print('state_of_mind_kinds', som_kinds)
print('\nOURA')
oura=json.loads((root/'oura_sleep_raw.json').read_text())
print('sleep count', len(oura['sleep']['data']))
for k,v in list(oura['sleep']['data'][0].items()):
    if isinstance(v,dict): print(k, 'dict keys', list(v.keys()), 'items len', len(v.get('items',[])))
    else: print(k, type(v).__name__, v)
print('\nPLAID')
plaid=json.loads((root/'plaid_transactions.json').read_text())
print('accounts', len(plaid['accounts']), 'transactions', len(plaid['transactions']))
print('transaction date range', plaid['transactions'][0]['date'], plaid['transactions'][-1]['date'])
print('\nMARKDOWN COUNTS')
for name in ['gp_visit_notes.md','imessage_threads.md','journal_entries.md']:
    text=(root/name).read_text()
    print(name, 'headers2', len(re.findall(r'^## ', text, flags=re.M)), 'dated h3', len(re.findall(r'^### \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', text, flags=re.M)))
result_df=pl.DataFrame({'status':['diagnostic_complete']})"}

messages.content: Calendar recurrence is the main place where “all relevant data” needs judgment because several events repeat indefinitely. I’m going to expand recurring VEVENTs through the export date window so the table has actual timestamps instead of only RRULE templates.

import json, polars as pl
root=Path(DATA_DIR)
oura=json.loads((root/'oura_sleep_raw.json').read_text())
first=oura['sleep']['data'][0]
print(first.get('readiness'))
print('sample hrv item', first['hrv']['items'][0])
# list all keys in sleep objects and readiness contributor keys
keys=set(); contrib=set(); movement_types=set()
for s in oura['sleep']['data']:
    keys.update(s.keys())
    r=s.get('readiness') or {}
    contrib.update((r.get('contributors') or {}).keys())
    mv=s.get('movement_30_sec')
    movement_types.add(type(mv).__name__)
print('all sleep keys', sorted(keys))
print('contributors', sorted(contrib))
print('movement types', movement_types)
result_df=pl.DataFrame({'status':['oura_inspected']})"}
